body:
## Ask

Capture **everything a forge actually contains** — issues, issue comments, PR comments, reviews and review threads, timeline events, labels, milestones, releases and asset manifests, check runs and statuses, discussions, rulesets and branch protections, repository metadata, workflow-run records — into a **completely lossless record of the entire system's state at any given moment in time**, stored in **the ledger**, so the whole thing is reconstructible and **completely transferable no matter what software you are running it with**.

This is the antithesis of the Constitution's named fear — *the lock-in with no migration path*. When the forge's entire state lives in the ledger in a forge-neutral schema, the forge becomes a replaceable renderer of state the project owns.

## Shape

- **`vibey-gh forge-snapshot`**: walks the forge API and emits every artifact class as append-only, forge-neutral records — plain structured text (12.a: meaning survives every stack), each record content-hashed, the capture hash-chained (the corpus-index pattern of #259 generalized to live state). Incremental via since-cursors; a full capture and a day's delta use one schema.
- **Forge-neutral nouns**: change-request, not PR; the same abstract vocabulary #243 defines — captured once, replayable anywhere. Snapshot on GitHub, restore on Forgejo: migration becomes `snapshot → replay`, and the fully-local deployment (#243's sovereign rung) inherits its entire history, not just its code.
- **Into the ledger**: records flow to the vibey ledger through an adapter interface, tiered per [vibey#114](https://github.com/adammatthewsteinberger/vibey/issues/114) — the hot window raw, history aggressively-and-losslessly compressed, the archival node holding everything since inception. Governance events (ratifications, supersessions) land immutably, which is the evidentiary substrate Articles IV.5–6 and V.4 assume.
- **Searchable**: once forge state is ledger state, [#247's explorer](https://github.com/adammatthewsteinberger/vibey-gh/issues/247) searches the project's ENTIRE history — every comment, every review, every decision — one search box over law, ledger, and forge alike (7.a: anyone, no matter who; human consumption first).
- **Lossless is testable**: the acceptance proof is bit-for-bit round-tripping — snapshot, restore into a clean forge, snapshot again, identical records (IDs mapped, content identical). Anything the schema cannot round-trip is a named, documented exclusion, never a silent one.

## Acceptance

- Every artifact class a forge exposes via API is captured or named as excluded with a reason — nothing silently dropped.
- Point-in-time reconstruction: given the ledger, the full state of issues/PRs/comments/releases *as of any captured moment* is derivable.
- The round-trip proof above, demonstrated GitHub → Forgejo on a real repository.
- Zero new runtime dependencies; the schema documented never-lost style; snapshot runs offline against a local forge.

Doctrine: 10.a (the forge's state now survives the forge), 12.a (translatability — the schema is plain structured text), 7.a (searchable by anyone), Article I (the lock-in fear answered), vibey#114 + #243 + #247 (this unifies all three epics into one migration-proof whole).

Made-With: Made with ❤️ by [Vibey](https://adammatthewsteinberger.github.io/vibey/), Developed by [Adam Matthew Steinberger](https://vibewithadam.matthewsteinberger.com/) ([@adammatthewsteinberger](https://github.com/adammatthewsteinberger/)).

## Triage — 2026-09-17 (`develop` @ f2467910, v0.8.0)

**Status: NOT STARTED** · size **XL** · confidence high

**The ask, as read:** Add a `vibey-gh forge-snapshot` that walks the forge API and emits every artifact class (issues, comments, reviews, timeline events, labels, milestones, releases, check runs, discussions, rulesets, repo metadata, workflow runs) as content-hashed, hash-chained, forge-neutral append-only records into the vibey ledger, with incremental cursors and a GitHub→Forgejo round-trip proof.

### Evidence in the tree
- src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/cli.py:929 — `sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)`; the registered subcommands through line 1290 are check, install, version, trailer(-key), conventional(-check), merge-train, pr-automation, issue-automation, conversation, github-release, promote, realign, reconcile-branches, rulesets, yank, local, doc, tidy, local-authority, failover, ci, marketplace, sovereign, fit, paper, book, latex, recommend and the five surface adapters — there is no `forge-snapshot`
- src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/surfaces.py:17 — the `CAPABILITIES` tuple lists 14 capabilities; no snapshot/capture/export capability exists, so nothing projects through the SDK/CLI/API/MCP/webhook surfaces either
- grep -rni 'ledger' src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/ returns zero hits — there is no ledger adapter interface, no writer, and no ledger import anywhere in the forge tool
- src/vibey/domain/ledger.py:18 — `class EventKind(StrEnum)` enumerates 25 kinds (SessionSeeded … DeploymentDeclined), all orchestration lifecycle; there is no forge-artifact kind (no issue, comment, review, release, check-run or ruleset record type)
- src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/github_state.py:2 — the only durable forge state the codebase keeps is "Durable automation state carried in exactly one GitHub comment": a JSON blob hidden in an HTML comment per PR/issue. That is an automation cursor, the opposite of a lossless capture, and it lives inside the forge it is supposed to survive
- src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/rulesets.py:2 — "Reconcile GitHub repository rulesets from `.vibey-gh.toml`" pushes declared config *into* the forge; no module reads forge state *out* into a neutral record
- …and 3 more

### What is actually left
- Define the forge-neutral record schema as plain structured text: change-request, thread, comment, review, review-thread, timeline-event, label, milestone, release, asset-manifest, check-run, status, discussion, ruleset, branch-protection, repository-metadata, workflow-run — each with a content hash and a chained capture hash
- Add a forge read-port interface in vibey-gh (per ADR-0016: interface file beside the class) with a GitHub adapter built on the existing `gh_json()` helper in github_state.py:26
- Add a second adapter (Forgejo) — the acceptance proof requires GitHub → Forgejo, so one implementation is not enough
- Implement `vibey-gh forge-snapshot` as a CLI subparser AND register it in surfaces.py `CAPABILITIES` so it reaches all five surfaces
- Implement incremental since-cursors so a full capture and a day's delta share one schema
- Define the ledger adapter interface and implement the writer — vibey-gh declares `dependencies = []`, so the adapter must be an interface there and the concrete ledger writer must live in vibey's infrastructure/
- Add the forge-artifact event kinds (or a distinct forge-record table) to the vibey ledger, with a point-in-time reconstruction query: state of issues/PRs/comments/releases as of any captured moment
- Build the restore/replay path that writes captured records back into a clean forge, mapping IDs
- …and 3 more

### Blockers
- The issue routes records "into the ledger … tiered per vibey#114" — #114 is not-started, so the stated storage target does not exist (a first cut could land in the current single heap `event` table, but that contradicts the issue's own design)
- The GitHub→Forgejo round-trip acceptance needs a real Forgejo instance and a real repository; no such fixture or adapter exists in the tree
- The forge-neutral vocabulary is defined by a sibling issue (#243) that is not resolved here, so the noun set is undecided
- Cross-package placement is constrained: vibey-gh is stdlib-only with `dependencies = []`, and vibey's `domain/` forbids `vibey_bootstrap` by name — the adapter seam has to be designed around both rules (CLAUDE.md non-negotiables; ADR-0017)

**Depends on:** #114

**Notes:** Zero code. The ask is also three epics fused into one (schema + snapshot tool + ledger adapter + restore + cross-forge proof), which is exactly what the automated solver reported failing on in the issue's first comment ("a request too large to complete in one attempt"). Splitting it — schema first, then GitHub capture, then the ledger adapter, then restore/round-trip — is the concrete path forward.


<sub>Automated triage pass: every open issue re-read against the tree at `develop@f2467910`, each verdict then attacked by an independent verifier whose job was to refute it. Supersedes the 2026-09-15 triage, which was measured at 0.7.0.</sub>

**Status: PARTIAL · planning size: XL**

Forge snapshot and hash-chained JSONL capture exist, along with provider adapters. The requested append-only ledger integration, point-in-time reconstruction/replay across all artifact classes, and verified GitHub-to-Forgejo round trip are not yet complete.
